turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

Since the training data’s yield‑strength values top out around **860–910 MPa** (well below the 1051 MPa target), the "closest‑to‑1051" candidates are simply those whose composition/processing profile most closely resembles the **highest‑strength training samples** (quench‑and‑temper, wrought route, moderate Cr/Ni, low‑to‑moderate Co, high aging_time, moderate cooling‑rate, solutionizing_temp ≈1100‑1150 °C).

**Key high‑strength training analogs used as reference points** (target MPa):

| target | C | Cr | Ni | Co | Mo | ST | AT | agingTime | CR | HT/route |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|863.93|0.33|5.81|10.40|0.92|0.98|1110.6|550.3|46.9|28.9|quench_temper/wrought|
|771.94|0.15|18.91|17.31|3.14|4.07|1124.4|643.2|25.3|48.5|solution_aged/cast|
|737.73|0.38|16.27|0.92|3.35|1.30|1151.3|543.8|20.2|26.3|quench_temper/cast|
|734.09|0.20|5.38|8.81|5.00|1.33|1232.3|524.9|35.1|11.1|quench_temper/wrought|
|726.38|0.26|13.60|12.71|4.49|3.21|1081.8|632.9|31.1|83.2|quench_temper/wrought|

**Nearest‑neighbor matching in the pool** (weighted‑distance / kNN‑style estimate) shows two candidates almost overlapping the top‑performing training sample (target ≈864 MPa):

- **c017** – Cr 7.65, Ni 10.12, Co 0.86, Mo 1.41, ST 1107.9, AT 529.1, agingTime 49.3, CR 38.1 (quench_temper/wrought) → extremely close to the 863.93 MPa exemplar → estimated ≈ 840‑850 MPa.
- **c094** – Cr 5.99, Ni 8.08, Co 1.99, Mo 0.47, ST 1129.1, AT 512.5, agingTime 50, CR 34.3 (quench_temper/wrought) → also very close to the same exemplar → estimated ≈ 830‑840 MPa.

The next tier of candidates (still quench_temper/wrought, similar Cr‑Ni‑Co‑Mo ranges but slightly larger deviations) give somewhat lower but still high predicted strengths:

- **c060** (Cr 8.87, Ni 7.63, Co 1.80, Mo 2.34, AT 551.2, agingTime 36.1) → ≈795 MPa
- **c022** (Cr 3.64, Ni 12.54, Co 3.75, Mo 1.68, AT 570.5, agingTime 31.8) → ≈780 MPa
- **c082** (Cr 6.47, Ni 9.45, Co 6.34, Mo 2.09, AT 525.9, agingTime 37.3) → ≈779 MPa

These five candidates are the closest matches (highest predicted yield strength, hence nearest to the 1051 MPa target) among the 100 pool entries.

Final: c017, c094, c060, c022, c082
